newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Progressive sees restoration of dividend.
newsitem.headline: Progressive sees restoration of dividend.

text.p: Progressive Enterprises Ltd Chairman Don Humphreys told the annual meeting on Friday the company expected to restore payment of an interim dividend at the end of the first half.

"The group is trading profitably. On the basis of the first quarter's results, sales for November and forecast results for the remainder of the year, I am pleased to report that the group is expecting to restore payment of an interim dividend at the completion of the first half's results," Humphreys said.
Progressive, a supermarket chain, is 57 percent-owned by Foodland Associated.

Humphreys said the sale of 17 Georgie Pie restaurants to McDonalds for NZ$25.5 million became unconditional on November 7. The transaction resulted in assets being transferred in excess of book value.
"We are now well into the implementation phase with restaurants being handed over and substantial cash flows received in return.
The last of the restaurants would be handed over on April 1.
Disposal of the remaining restaurant network and the manufacturing facility was under review and expressions of interest had been received from a number parties.
Humphreys said there was a strong focus on developing a portfolio of high performing sites.
In addition to the Georgie Pie property sales, the divestment programme continued with sales of property totalling NZ$16.4 million becoming unconditional since balance date.
Term debt fell to NZ$173 million at the end of the first quarter compared with NZ$207 million at the same time last year.
Interest cover covenants were met at the end of the first quarter and were forecast to improve as the year progressed.
